newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rostelekom votes on doubling authorised shares.
newsitem.headline: Rostelekom votes on doubling authorised shares.

text.p: Russian national telecoms company Rostelekom will give its board of directors authority to issue shares doubling current capital if shareholders approve a new charter this week, the company said on Wednesday.
Rostelekom has no plans to issue new shares, securities department head Igor Kochezhkov told Reuters, but he said the new charter would double authorised capital and allow new issues by the board.
"In principle the board of directors could deal with that issue. In principle a shareholders meeting would not be needed to approve the size of a new issue," he said.
The new charter must be approved by 75 percent of shareholders in a vote conducted by mail ending on Friday. The company will not convene a shareholders' meeting.
Kochezhkov said Rostelekom would seek shareholder approval for any new share issue, despite the lack of such provisions in the draft charter.
"This would not be done under the table or quickly -- it would be approved by shareholders," Kochezhkov said of a share issue. "There are no such plans today."
Rostelekom is one of the most liquid Russian shares.
Kochezhkov declined to say whether Svyazinvest, the government holding company which has a majority stake in Rostelekom, supported the plan.
Foreign shareholders have about 30 percent of company shares.
